more_info.overview: Beeswax is used as a stabilizer in food. Its technological role is to help maintain the structure of food.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include edible ices, entire fresh fruit and vegetables, cocoa and chocolate products as covered by directive 2000/36/ec, other confectionery including breath freshening micro-sweets. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Beeswax is recovered by melting honeycomb walls with hot water and removing foreign material. White beeswax is made by bleaching yellow beeswax.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: Derived from honeybee wax; it is unsuitable for vegan diets. Vegetarian acceptance depends on whether bee products are included. Halal and kosher certification was not established by the specification.
